title: TVF's Other Village Show Is Back. And It Might Be the Sleeper Hit Diaspora Audiences Have Been Waiting For.
excerpt: Gram Chikitsalay Season 2 drops on Prime Video June 23. Amol Parashar returns as the idealistic rural doctor, Bhojpuri superstar Nirahua joins as the new antagonist, and yes — Panchayat's Banrakas and Binod make a cameo.
body:
If you loved **Panchayat**, you owe it to yourself to know about its quieter sibling.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=6YkxIy5QkwA</youtube>

**Gram Chikitsalay** premiered on Amazon Prime Video in May 2025 with almost no buzz and walked away with something far more valuable: genuine audience affection. The show — created by the same **TVF** (The Viral Fever) stable that gave us the Mishras of Phulera — follows **Dr. Prabhat Mishra** (played by **Amol Parashar**), an idealistic young doctor posted to a crumbling Primary Health Centre in the fictional village of Bhathkandi. Think Panchayat, but instead of a panchayat secretary navigating small-town politics, it's a physician navigating small-town healthcare. Same warmth. Same frustration. Same irresistible pull of a place that slowly becomes home.

The Season 2 trailer dropped on Friday, and within hours, it was trending. The reason is obvious the moment you press play.

## What's New This Season

Dr. Prabhat has earned the village's trust — the hard part is supposed to be over. But when he discovers a chronic shortage of medicines at the PHC, he decides to go to war with the system. Specifically, with a man called **Babu Saheb**, played by **Dinesh Lal Yadav** — better known as **Nirahua**, the undisputed king of Bhojpuri cinema.



> **"He has experienced some good wins, but a whole new set of challenges comes his way." — Amol Parashar

Nirahua's entry is inspired casting."**


> "In the latest chapter, my character's journey in Bhathkandi moves forward in unexpected ways. He has experienced some good wins, but a whole new set of challenges comes his way." — Amol Parashar

Nirahua's entry is inspired casting. He brings a completely different energy — louder, more political, more rooted in the power structures of rural India — and his Bhojpuri-inflected Hindi performance is already being praised in early reactions. If Season 1 was about an outsider learning to listen, Season 2 looks like it's about that same outsider learning to fight.

The returning cast is intact: **Vinay Pathak** as the lovably unhelpful Chetan Kumar, **Akansha Ranjan Kapoor** as the sharp-tongued Dr. Gargi, and a full complement of village regulars. But here's the detail that has the internet buzzing: **Banrakas and Binod** — the beloved side characters from *Panchayat* — reportedly make cameo appearances, placing both shows in a shared TVF rural universe.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

For NRIs on Prime Video in the US, UK, Canada, and beyond, Gram Chikitsalay fills a very specific gap. The Indian OTT landscape is dominated by crime thrillers, spy sagas, and urban dramas — all of which are excellent, but none of which scratch the itch for the kind of grounded, slice-of-life storytelling that made *Panchayat* a phenomenon.

This is a show about a man trying to get bandages and paracetamol to a village that the government has forgotten. There are no gunfights. No twists. Just the slow, maddening comedy of trying to do something good in a system designed to make you give up. If that doesn't hit different when you're 8,000 miles from the village your parents grew up in, nothing will.

The show is available in Hindi on Prime Video globally — no geo-restrictions, no waiting for an international release window.

## The TVF Formula

Created by **Arunabh Kumar** and **Deepak Kumar Mishra**, directed by **Lalitam Anand**, and written by the **Vaibhav Suman–Shreya Srivastava** duo, Gram Chikitsalay shares Panchayat's DNA without being a copy. Where Panchayat leans comedic, Gram Chikitsalay carries a sharper social edge — the healthcare system it depicts isn't just inefficient, it's actively hostile to the people it's supposed to serve.

Prime Video India's content head **Manish Menghani** put it plainly: "We are seeing a growing appetite not just for authentic urban narratives, but increasingly for stories rooted in rural India as well."

He's not wrong. And on June 23, the evidence arrives.

*Gram Chikitsalay Season 2 premieres June 23, 2026, on Amazon Prime Video worldwide.*
